limitations: Pinned to the released catalog tag v4.22.0 of apache/camel-kamelets (retrieved 2026-09-18); a newer catalog is a new pin, never an automatic upgrade.
The Camel route template, dataTypes block and Maven dependency list are preserved as inert data: nothing is evaluated, resolved or deployed.
A source Kamelet's delivery transport is a Camel component, not an HTTP webhook, so the event descriptor is transport unsupported with the native scheme preserved.
No live catalog fetch was performed from a test; fixtures are locally authored documents shaped exactly like the released ones.
workItems.notes: Bounded YAML goes through the shared parseBoundedDocument (yaml 2.9.0, core schema, uniqueKeys, merge keys off, resolveKnownTags off, bounded maxAliasCount) rather than a second parser. Secret classification follows the catalog's own markers first (format: password, x-descriptors urn:camel:group:credentials or the OLM password descriptor) and only then a name heuristic, which is reported as a compatibility issue so the inference is visible. A credential's declared default is dropped and the drop is a blocking issue. Credential custody is declared external-execution-broker, because a Camel runner holds and uses these values and Ceremony never does; no API-key or OAuth method is invented for a route template.

limitations: Binding directions are taken from the supported-bindings component reference (docs.dapr.io, runtime v1.18, retrieved 2026-09-18) for the sixteen types that page states; any other component type is reported direction unknown and unverified rather than guessed.

There is no discover dimension: Dapr documents no sidecar component-inventory endpoint, and asking one for its loaded components would be the unauthenticated inventory surface this adapter exists to refuse.
There is no verify dimension: a sidecar exposes no account or identity endpoint, so connectivity could only be relabelled as identity.
Dapr defines no idempotency key for a binding invocation, so an interrupted write is journalled indeterminate and never retried automatically.

A Dapr input delivery carries no provider event id; deduplication therefore uses host-assigned identity, and the app API token carries no timestamp so this leg cannot be replay-bounded by the signature itself.
Disconnect is local only: Dapr offers a platform caller no operation to delete a component, unload it from a sidecar or revoke a sidecar token.
workItems.notes: The runtime binding restricts four things at once: the single approved sidecar destination, the component names allowed for output invocation, the operation verbs allowed per component, and the per-call metadata keys. The bound operation's path template must equal the route rebuilt from its own approved component name, so a template naming another component is a policy failure rather than a differently-addressed call. An unauthenticated sidecar is admissible only when the binding declares it explicitly and the destination's network class is loopback-fixture; a public or approved-private sidecar without DAPR_API_TOKEN is refused with configuration-required, which is the concrete form of 'never a generic unauthenticated browser proxy'. The input receiver authenticates with the app API token (dapr-api-token, APP_API_TOKEN) in constant time, and is offered both as an adapter EventPort and as a VendorVerifierPort for the shared webhook receiver.

limitations: Provision, deprovision, update, bind and unbind are not implemented: the module contains no request builder for them and every bound operation must be a GET with effect read, so the default profile cannot issue a state-changing request even if a binding asked it to.

Fetching an instance or a binding is attempted only when the reviewed catalog declared instances_retrievable or bindings_retrievable. The specification defines no error for calling an unsupported fetch endpoint, so an absent flag is reported as a native limitation and the endpoint is never probed.
Paid plans are recorded as out of scope: no plan change and no provisioning of a non-free plan is available here.
A fetched instance is the broker's assertion about its own record; the verification claim says so and asserts nothing about the underlying resource, and no permissions are inferred.
Binding rotation, volume mounts, syslog drains and route services are described but not exercised; only their presence is reported.
Basic authentication is the specification's default platform-to-broker mechanism and the only one implemented; out-of-band mechanisms are explicitly out of scope in the specification itself.
workItems.notes: Pinned to the released tag v2.17 of openservicebrokerapi/servicebroker (spec.md, retrieved 2026-09-18); the repository's master copy is labelled as possibly containing unreleased changes and is deliberately not the pin. Every request sends X-Broker-API-Version: 2.17 and a fresh X-Broker-API-Request-Identity; X-Broker-API-Originating-Identity is sent only for a human-initiated request and carries a SHA-256 pseudonym of tenant and subject, never a host identifier. A 412 from a broker is reported unsupported rather than retried at a lower version. Credentials returned by a binding fetch are stored through CredentialCustodyPort and the result carries a credentialRef plus the credential key names; no credential value appears in any result, projection or error.

limitations: The default KameletHostRunnerPort is unavailable and fail-closed; its reason names that no Camel runner is configured and that Ceremony starts no JVM, resolves no dependency and deploys no integration.
A deployment whose runtime class is browser cannot be given a runner at all: construction throws, so no code path exists in which a browser-only deployment reports local execution.
A configured remote runner is unavailable until its signing-secret configuration is present; an unsigned delegation is never sent.

The delegation signature is a host-internal scheme (HMAC-SHA256 over v1:timestamp:nonce:descriptor-digest), not a vendor protocol; it is not a claim of interoperability with any Camel distribution's own API.
workItems.notes: The run descriptor names the Kamelet, its catalog release, the non-secret parameter values the host approved and the host configuration names holding the secret ones. A credential value never enters a descriptor, an export or a request body. The invoke path journals the effect before delegating and records indeterminate when the runner call fails, so an interrupted run is reconcilable rather than silently retried.

limitations: All evidence is protocol-fixture. No vendor account, broker, sidecar or Camel runtime was contacted, and nothing here is live or vendor-certified.

The three doubles are written from the published documentation and decide conformance themselves; none of them calls the implementation under test, including the Camel runner double, which recomputes the delegation HMAC with node:crypto rather than using the signing helper.
workItems.notes: 74 tests over the three areas cover fixture catalogs, configured-runner operations, invalid and missing credentials, unknown component and binding names, omitted optional retrieval capabilities, event authentication and rotation, and unavailable-runtime reporting. Hostile YAML (duplicate keys, an unsupported tag, an alias bomb, a merge key) is refused within bounds with sanitized codes that quote nothing from the document.

integrationPatches.description: Register the three adapters where the host builds its ConnectorAdapterRegistry: createCamelKameletAdapter(options) from src/server/connectors/formats/camel-kamelet/index.ts, createDaprAdapter(options) from src/server/connectors/providers/dapr/index.ts, and createOpenServiceBrokerAdapter(options) from src/server/connectors/providers/open-service-broker/index.ts. Adapter ids are camel-kamelet, dapr and open-service-broker. All three take only optional arguments and default to safe behaviour: the Kamelet adapter defaults to an unavailable runner, and Dapr and the broker default to protocol-fixture evidence.

A deployment whose runtime class is browser must construct the Kamelet adapter as createCamelKameletAdapter({ deploymentRuntime: "browser" }). Passing a runner alongside that throws ConnectorError("unsupported", { detail: "kamelet.runner.browser-deployment" }) by design; do not catch and ignore it.

Register createDaprVendorVerifier() from src/server/connectors/providers/dapr/verifier.ts with the shared webhook receiver under vendor id "dapr-app-api-token" so a Dapr input binding is received through the existing authenticated receiver rather than a parallel route. Its secrets resolver should return the host's DAPR_APP_API_TOKEN values (several to allow rotation).

Mount two routes for Dapr input bindings on the application side: OPTIONS /<component> answering the sidecar's startup subscription probe with the status from daprInputSubscriptionStatus(settings, component) (200 to subscribe, 404 to decline), and POST /<component> delivering into the receiver. The route, not the request, decides which component was addressed: pass the matched path segment to createDaprEventPort({ resolveInputBinding }) or call verifyDaprInputDelivery(ctx, { bindingName, delivery }) directly. A header naming the component must never be trusted for this.
No change requested. All three modules are server-only and must stay out of the default browser bundle; none of them is referenced from src/core.

unmet.item: Live catalog retrieval from camel.apache.org or the GitHub release tag at runtime
unmet.reason: Tests have no internet by rule, and a live fetch adds no contract this importer does not already exercise from bytes. A deployment that wants a live catalog binds the release URL as an approved destination; that path is untested here and is recorded as such.

unmet.item: Dapr gRPC transport and the Dapr Actors, Workflow and Conversation building blocks
unmet.reason: Out of scope for BIND-02, which is component and binding metadata plus the HTTP output-binding and input-receiver profiles. Non-binding components import as descriptions with a blocking issue saying they have no invocation profile here.

unmet.item: Binding rotation (PUT with predecessor_binding_id) and the maintenance_info update flow
unmet.reason: Both are mutating operations. They belong to a provisioning profile that this swarm deliberately does not implement, and adding a request builder for them would remove the structural guarantee that no state-changing request can be issued.

externalEffectsPerformed.effect: Read public specification and documentation pages over HTTPS during research
externalEffectsPerformed.note: Read-only public documentation. No account was created, no credential issued, no package installed, no image pulled, no container or JVM started, and no vendor API was called with credentials.
